answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small deposit that only unlocks after peers attest its useful work over time, so fake identities cost real money and time to maintain. Reputation should spread like a whisper across a network of independent verifiers rather than from one central registry, making it hard to fabricate at scale. Like layers of shale pressed into a mesa, each attestation builds on the last, and an identity that appears overnight with no history of contribution stands out immediately and earns nothing.
